blocks.text: PIANO REMOVAL PRICING
What Actually Determines an Aurora Piano Removal Quote

c: The starting point is the piano itself. An upright or console is the more straightforward job — heavy, but usually manageable without full disassembly beyond clearing a doorway. A baby grand adds real complexity, since the legs and lid typically need to come off before it fits through a standard opening, meaning more time and a coordinated lift. A full grand piano is the most involved version, with legs, lid and often the pedal lyre separating from the body, each section still heavy enough to need multiple people carrying it carefully.

What layers on top of that baseline in Aurora is the property itself, though never in a way that changes the number. A heritage home near the village core might have narrower original doorways that call for extra patience during disassembly. A newer home in Bayview or Wellington East usually has a more generous modern floor plan that moves faster once the route is confirmed. A larger property on the Aurora Estates or around the Hills of St Andrew might mean a longer route across the grounds to reach the truck. All three get sorted out honestly at the free walkthrough, and none of them shows up as a separate line item.

Aurora Piano Removal Questions People Actually Ask

items.q: Do you remove pianos on larger Aurora Estates or Hills of St Andrew properties?
a: Yes — bigger lots and pianos are regular work for us, with the same standard of grounds and driveway protection applied whatever the property’s scale.

items.q: How careful are you around older homes near Aurora Village?
a: Genuinely careful. Original features that stay get protected, and the work moves at a pace that respects the property’s age.

items.q: How much does piano removal cost in Aurora?
a: Pricing is confirmed free at the walkthrough based on the piano’s size and access — never the neighbourhood.

items.q: What's actually involved in moving a grand or baby grand piano?
a: Legs, the lid and sometimes the pedal lyre come off to fit through doorways and stairwells, and the piano moves on proper piano boards.

items.q: Do you charge extra for stairs?
a: No. Narrow staircases and multi-floor moves are factored into one flat quote at the walkthrough.

items.q: What happens to the piano once it's removed?
a: Donation partners are checked first for pianos that still play; only pianos beyond use go to recycling.

items.q: Can you remove a piano the same day I call?
a: Often, yes — trucks run seven days a week, 6AM to 11PM.

items.q: Can you clear more than one item in a single visit?
a: Yes — a piano and other furniture on the same property can be scoped and quoted together.
